    Lemma 5.2 in its abstract form #

    mesh-deformations.tex (lem:deletion-brick): "Let 𝒟 be a full additive subcategory of a finite-length k-linear abelian category, closed under images and direct summands. Assume finite-dimensional Hom spaces and Krull–Schmidt decomposition. For any set Σ of indecomposable isomorphism classes, every nonempty quotient ind 𝒟/[Σ] has an object whose endomorphism ring is a division algebra. If all residue division algebras are k, the quotient has a brick."

    Proof (as in the source): among the objects of ind 𝒟 outside Σ, take one, X, minimal among subobjects of a fixed object (the descending chain condition, IsArtinianObject). A radical endomorphism f of X is not epi (an epi endomorphism of an object with finite-dimensional endomorphisms is invertible, isUnit_of_epi), so it factors through its proper image; the indecomposable summands of the image are smaller, lie in 𝒟 by image-closure, hence in Σ. Conversely a map through Σ is a radical endomorphism: an invertible one would make X a summand of an indecomposable object of Σ (not_isUnit_through). Hence End(X)/[Σ](X, X) = End(X)/rad, the residue division algebra (deletionBrick). Indecomposable objects are those with local endomorphism rings (Krull–Schmidt); closure under summands is not needed.

      Lemma 5.2 (lem:deletion-brick), abstract form. In a k-linear abelian category with finite-dimensional Hom spaces in which every object is Artinian, let 𝒟 be a subcategory closed under isomorphisms and images, in which every object is a finite direct sum of objects with local endomorphism rings (Krull–Schmidt), and let Σ be a set of objects with local endomorphism rings, closed under isomorphisms. If some indecomposable object of 𝒟 lies outside Σ, there is one, X, such that the endomorphisms of X factoring through Σ are exactly the non-invertible ones: the endomorphism ring of X in ind 𝒟/[Σ] is the residue division algebra End(X)/rad. If that residue algebra is k, X is a brick of the quotient.
